sourceMathEvidence: A real cubic P and real linear Q satisfy divisibility of P·Q by (x²−6x+10)(x−2), an all-x identity F=P+Q², sign constraints, and P(2)=0.
solutionMathEvidence: The irreducible quadratic cannot divide linear Q, so it divides P. The decisive coefficient equations come from reducing P modulo x²−6x+10 with x²≡6x−10 and requiring its linear remainder to vanish. P(2)=0 and sign tests then select m=−2,n=3, yielding the requested value −2.
reason: The structural gate is division of P by a quadratic divisor and zeroing its remainder coefficients. The linear-root condition P(2)=0 is a later constraint and does not own the primary type. The L3 나머지정리 draft refers to P(a) for a linear divisor; this item instead performs a degree-two quotient/remainder reduction. Therefore the curriculum draft parent 다항식의 나눗셈 is the narrowest faithful owner, while the polynomial factor and root relations remain item-level evidence for later L4/CrossConcept review.
